intelligence.essence:
- **HIS WORDS, VERBATIM:** "all of a sudden it separates. All of your spaces, business, and all of a sudden it's nine app slash join us. Just random no explanation of why the presentation is different or the boxes are different" — "merge both presentations together make the ultimate"
- **THE DEFECT:** halfway down the page the presentation changes for no reason — different boxes, different actions ("click link copy link link or open link" on one kind, no click-to-open or copy-link on the other). The reader cannot tell why, because there is no why.
- **THE FIX:** ONE ultimate board design for both. The sections are separated and NAMED — pages vs Smart Links — so the reader always knows what they're looking at. Actions are consistent across all boards: page boards get Open in the same style as Copy/Open.
- **THE RULE INSIDE IT:** a change of presentation must have a reason the reader can see. If two things look different, the difference must mean something; if it means nothing, it is one design.
- **SCOPE:** the Dashboard boards page — page boards and Smart Link boards alike.
intelligence.human_view: Scroll down and suddenly the page changes its mind: one kind of board looks one way, another kind looks another way, and nothing tells you why — different boxes, different buttons, no explanation. It feels random because it is random. His fix is to merge both presentations into one ultimate design: every board looks like every other board, and the only difference is the section it sits in — pages here, Smart Links there, each named, so you always know what you're looking at. Same actions on every board, too: if a link board has Copy and Open, a page board has Open in the same style. One design, named sections — the page stops changing its mind halfway down.
intelligence.child_view: The page had two kinds of boards that looked all different from each other, for no reason at all — like two different games mixed up in one box. So now they all become one kind of board, the very best one, and they're sorted into groups with names on them, so you always know what you're looking at. Same buttons on every board, too.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the page kept changing how its boards looked halfway down, love, with no reason for it at all — one kind had this button, the other kind had that one. Now they all become one beautiful board, dear, the very best one, sorted into sections with proper names, so you always know what you're looking at. Same buttons everywhere, nice and tidy.
intelligence.ai_view: This is the one-design law: a system has one language, and a change in the language must mean something. It connects to SN-2519 (one sequence for all boards — the color is the position, the same rule everywhere) and to SN-2525/2526 (the boards page has a structure the reader can hold in their head — named sections, one headliner). Two presentations with no reason is the page disagreeing with itself, and a page that disagrees with itself cannot be read with confidence. The merge is not a compromise between the two designs — it is the ultimate one, taking the best of both, and the sections are the naming that makes the one design legible: the reader always knows which system they are in.
intelligence.what_it_means:
- **ONE BOARD DESIGN:** page boards and Smart Link boards share a single ultimate design.
- **SECTIONS SEPARATED AND NAMED:** pages vs Smart Links, so the reader always knows what they're looking at.
- **ACTIONS CONSISTENT:** page boards get Open in the same style as Copy/Open — no board is missing the actions the others have.
